claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a continuous, mechanically robust passivating oxide layer.
As-deposited AlCrTiZrMo films can have a strongly amorphous initial structure.
Annealing AlCrTiZrMo at 800 °C for 1 h forms a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on its surface.
The dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer inhibits continued high-temperature oxidation of AlCrTiZrMo in air.
The oxide layer rapidly repassivates areas damaged by sliding.
The surface oxide layer mechanically reinforces the alloy microstructure against deformation and wear.
Annealing produces a refined microstructure that promotes in situ formation of the robust oxide during tribocorrosion.
A stable, dense annealed microstructure together with increased hardness and elastic-modulus-related properties improves resistance to external mechanical damage.
AlCrTiZrMo annealed at 800 °C for 1 h has better tribocorrosion resistance than the as-deposited and lower-temperature-annealed states.
Relative to the baseline, the 800 °C annealed film will exhibit lower ΔOCP, lower coefficient of friction, and lower wear rate.

The performance improvements are caused specifically by continuity and mechanical robustness of the ZrTiO4 oxide rather than by the annealed substrate's dense microstructure and mechanical properties.
Low-temperature annealing is insufficient to provide the same reduction in ΔOCP, friction, and wear rate as annealing at 800 °C.
The protective effect should hold under moderate loads and temperatures that permit a stable oxide layer.
Extreme mechanical or thermal conditions can crack or spall the oxide and thereby eliminate the predicted tribocorrosion benefit.
